question: The famous tribal revolt of _________ took place in 1906 in Assam against British policies.
solution:
The correct answer is** Songram Sangma.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Songram Sangma**

 
 
• **​**One of the most important rebellions against the British in **Assam in 1906 **was led by Songram Sangma.
 
• The** British's exploitation** of the tribes deprives them of their **traditional forest rights,** which led to this revolt.
 
• The British **forcibly relocated** the tribal people who were dispersed within the **deep forests **to a small land where they could better control them.
 
• The tribal people relied on forests as a **source of income,** so the British laws governing forests had a significant impact on their lives.
 
• The British declared all forests to be **state property** and designated some as reserved, prohibiting tribal people from** hunting, cultivating,** or** fruit-collecting** in these areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other tribal movements**

 
 
• **Saflas** raided British plains subjects in **1835**, and they **revolted** once more between **1872 and 1973.**
 
• The Mishimis **murdered** Griffith, a **botanist**, and two missionaries in **1836.**
 
• There was a **Khampti** uprising in Assam from **1839 to 1842**, during which they attacked and killed British Agent **Adam White** and 80 other officers and soldiers.
 
• The **Syntengs** of the **Jaintia Hills** revolted from **1860 to 1862.**
